Let me look at the loop in `crash_safe_single_tx`:

```dafny
while i < |writes|
    decreases |writes| - i;
    invariant 0 <= i <= |writes|;
    invariant s.mem_len == |init_mem|;
    invariant s.mem_len == |end_mem|;
    invariant 0 <= s.num_entry <= i;
    invariant i * 2 < |s.log|;
    invariant 0 <= s.num_entry * 2 < |s.log|;
    invariant ghost_tx_inv(s);
    invariant old_mem_equiv(s);
    invariant init_mem == s.old_mem;
    invariant !crashed(s) ==> forall i :: 0 <= i < |s.mem| ==> s.mem[i] == end_mem[i];
```

The body does:
```dafny
    s := ghost_tx_write(s, writes[i].0, writes[i].1);
    end_mem := end_mem[writes[i].0 := writes[i].1];
    assert !crashed(s) ==> s.mem[writes[i].0] == writes[i].1;
    i := i + 1;
```

The problematic invariant is:
`!crashed(s) ==> forall i :: 0 <= i < |s.mem| ==> s.mem[i] == end_mem[i]`

The issue is: `ghost_tx_write` can crash (when countdown reaches 0). When it crashes, the mem write doesn't happen. But `end_mem` is updated unconditionally. So after a crash:
- `s.mem` doesn't have the new value at `writes[i].0`
- `end_mem` does have the new value at `writes[i].0`

But the invariant says `!crashed(s) ==> ...`. After a crash, `crashed(s)` is true (countdown = 0), so the implication is vacuously true. But wait - the next iteration, `s.countdown` is already 0, so `ghost_tx_write` will crash again (countdown stays 0). So `crashed(s)` remains true forever. The invariant would be vacuously true for all subsequent iterations.
